messages:
alice_support: FYI - Customer julia_cust (cust-902) opened a ticket: embeddings endpoint returning 1536-d vectors even though they pinned to the 1024-width variant last night. Started immediately after we applied the variant lock. Small repro attached.

julia_cust: Repro snippet I used:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-embed-2026:locked-1024","input":["hello world"]}' | jq .
```
Response shows: `embedding_length: 1536` and the array length matches that. We expected 1024.

alice_support: Logged with cust ticket #902. No config changes on their side besides the pinned model request. They said requests before the pin returned 1024. After pin, immediate swap.

ben_eng: Can you paste the minimal request/response JSON (no keys) and the model field they pinned to? Also which infra region? Sometimes alias fallback to a higher-dim variant happens when a pinned binary isn't available.

alice_support: Pasted minimal (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model":"open-embed-2026:locked-1024",
  "input":["test vector"]
}
```
Response header excerpt: `x-variant-resolved: open-embed-2026-v2` and body indicates vector length 1536. Region us-west-2.

carla_sre: Checking routing logs now. Quick theory: the locked tag may have been mapped to a runtime alias that points to a different quant/profile (v2) with 1536 dims due to a recent model upload. Asking deploy-bot for the resolution events around the lock time.

deploy-bot: [auto] model-alias-update detected: alias `open-embed-2026:locked-1024` -> candidate `open-embed-2026-v2` at 2026-11-09T03:12:08Z. Fallback triggered on node pool gpuprod-3 due to missing kernel for quant profile `q8_1024`.

ben_eng: That fallback line is the smoking gun. If the pinned variant couldn't be served on that pool, smart routing falls back to a compatible model - unfortunately the v2 variant has 1536 dims. Two follow-ups: 1) confirm whether the customer was routed to gpuprod-3 exclusively (we log routing_id in traces), 2) check batchpad/concat logic for multi-item requests (we've seen combined-batch pad expose different vectors but length should still be consistent).

alice_support: Traces show routing_id -> gpuprod-3 for their requests at 03:12-03:20. They only sent single-input requests. No batching on client.

carla_sre: I pulled the node logs. There's an error before fallback: `ERR kernel_missing: q8_1024 not found for model open-embed-2026:locked-1024`. Then the orchestrator selected `open-embed-2026-v2` as compatible. I've opened an ops ticket to pin the alias to the correct build on gpuprod-3 and to re-deploy the q8_1024 artifact.

ben_eng: Short-term mitigation: we can force route cust-902 to another pool that has the q8_1024 image (gpuprod-1) via a routing override. That will restore 1024 vectors. Long-term: need a pre-flight check when creating locks that verifies artifact availability in all pools in the customer's region.

alice_support: Communicated workaround to customer: route override to gpuprod-1 until ops confirms redeploy. Customer is OK but wants root cause and ETA.

julia_cust: Thanks - override worked, vectors now 1024. Can you confirm no downstream indexing corruption happened on our side? We ran a small reindex and saw slightly different distances but that's expected; want confirmation we won't see wider drift.

ben_eng: If you consumed 1536-d vectors into an index expecting 1024, you'll see shape mismatch errors or silent truncation depending on client side. Recommend reindex of any data ingested during the window. We'll provide a list of request timestamps for cust-902.

carla_sre: Ops ETA for q8_1024 redeploy to gpuprod-3: ~2 hours. Will post updates here when complete. Also filing a follow-up to add an alert when alias resolution results in a model with different embedding_dim than the alias metadata.

alice_support: Marking ticket P1 -> now customer satisfied with workaround. We should still follow up on process/alerts. Closing loop with product for pre-flight verification. :thumbsup:
